classification.difficultyReason: Derive the tangent at a symbolic point, extract its axis intercepts and recognise that their absolute lengths have a constant product across both branches.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $P\left(cp,\frac{c}{p}\right)$, where $c$ is a constant, lies on the hyperbola $xy=c^2$.

answer.worked:
Substitute the coordinates of $P$.

$$\begin{align*}xy&=(cp)\left(\frac{c}{p}\right)\\xy&=c^2.\end{align*}$$

Thus $P$ lies on the hyperbola.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw a sketch of the hyperbola and label any point $P$ on the curve.

answer.short: The branches lie in quadrants I and III and approach both axes. The sketch shows one choice of $P$.
answer.worked: Since $c^2>0$, $y=\frac{c^2}{x}$ has the same sign as $x$. Draw branches in quadrants I and III approaching both axes. Mark $P\left(cp,\frac{c}{p}\right)$ on either branch. The sketch shows the case $cp>0$.

spec.description: Two hyperbola branches, the marked point P on the first-quadrant branch, and dashed projections to symbolic coordinate labels. The blue curve and point distinguish the function from the black axes and guides.
spec.mathematics: The sketch uses representative display coordinates for xy=c² and a first-quadrant choice of P. The axes are asymptotes, and the point's coordinates are labelled symbolically as cp and c/p.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the tangent at $P$ has equation $x+p^2y=2cp$. Draw the tangent on your sketch.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=c^2x^{-1}\\y'&=-\frac{c^2}{x^2}\\y'\big|_{x=cp}&=-\frac{c^2}{(cp)^2}=-\frac{1}{p^2}.\end{align*}$$

Use this gradient and the coordinates of $P$.

$$\begin{align*}y-\frac{c}{p}&=-\frac{1}{p^2}(x-cp)\\p^2y-cp&=-x+cp\\x+p^2y&=2cp.\end{align*}$$

Add this line through $P$ to the sketch from part (b).

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 6(c), tangent construction requested in the prompt
spec.description: The complete sketch from part (b) with a solid black tangent through P. The projections remain dashed.
spec.mathematics: The tangent has the slope of the plotted reciprocal curve at P. Its axis intercepts are twice the corresponding coordinates of P, as required by x+p²y=2cp.

children.label: d
children.prompt: The tangent intersects the $x$ and $y$ axes at $A$ and $B$ respectively. Show that the area of $\triangle OAB$ will always be the same, regardless of where the tangent was drawn.

answer.short: The area is $2c^2$ square units. The intercept distances are $|2cp|$ and $\left|\frac{2c}{p}\right|$, so $p$ cancels.
answer.worked:
Setting $y=0$ gives $A=(2cp,0)$. Setting $x=0$ gives $B=\left(0,\frac{2c}{p}\right)$. The axes are perpendicular, so

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=\frac{1}{2}|2cp|\left|\frac{2c}{p}\right|\\\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=2c^2\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

The area depends only on the constant $c$.
